name: Chapter 6: Profitability, Growth and Liquidity — Mock-exam-calibrated MCQs (4–6 options)

questions.text: A firm reports net income €120m, assets €1,000m at the start of the year and €1,100m at year-end. Equity is €400m initially and €440m finally. Its ROA and ROE are approximately:

Consider the statements.
I. ROE can be affected by changes in financial leverage.
II. A high ROE is always evidence of low financial risk.
III. ROA combines profit and balance-sheet asset investment.
Which set is correct?

options.a: III only
options.d: I and III only

questions.text: A company has net profit margin 6%, asset turnover 1.5 and financial leverage 2.0. Its traditional DuPont ROE is:

Two firms have identical ROA of 8%. Firm A has financial leverage of 1.5 and Firm B has leverage of 3.0. Ignoring differences in accounting conventions, which statement is consistent with traditional DuPont?

options.a: ROE is 12% for A and 24% for B, with B more exposed to leverage risk.
options.b: ROE is 12% for both because their underlying operating returns are identical.
options.c: ROE is 12% for A and 24% for B, but no leverage conclusion is possible from the given balance-sheet information.
options.d: Both firms earn 8% ROE because net income is divided by assets rather than by equity.
options.e: ROE is 5.3% for A and 2.7% for B, with A more exposed to leverage risk.
options.f: ROE is 24% for A and 12% for B because leverage reduces equity returns.

questions.text: A business reports net income of −€25m, average assets €500m and average equity €125m. Under the chapter's ROA–leverage identity, ROE is:

options.a: +20%, because the denominator contains less equity.
options.b: −5%, with leverage improving the shareholder return because net income is negative.
options.c: −10%, because leverage is conventionally omitted from all calculations involving losses.
options.d: −20%, with leverage amplifying the negative return.
options.e: +5%, because a net loss creates a positive equity spread.
options.f: −5%, with leverage neutralizing the negative return.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Increasing leverage invariably reduces default risk if ROA is positive.
II. ROA can be expressed as profit margin multiplied by asset turnover.
III. ROE can be expressed as ROA multiplied by the equity multiplier.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.d: I and III only

questions.text: Company A has a 3% net margin and asset turnover of 2.5; Company B has a 15% margin and turnover of 0.5. What follows?

options.a: A earns 15% ROA and B earns 3% ROA because turnover is the dominant factor.
options.b: Both earn 7.5% ROA through contrasting profitability–asset productivity combinations.
options.c: Company A has higher ROA because its turnover is greater, even though its product margin is substantially lower.
options.d: Both have 7.5% ROA, but they necessarily have the same operating risk because ROA matches.
options.e: A earns 1.2% ROA and B earns 30% ROA because the two ratios must be divided.
options.f: Both earn 2.0% ROA because a high margin cancels a low asset turnover rate.

questions.text: A luxury-goods firm reports an unusually high profit margin but low asset turnover. Which explanation best fits the lecture?

options.a: Low turnover means the company must have a negative cash conversion cycle.
options.b: High margins can coexist with assets tied up in capital-intensive or low-volume operations.
options.c: High margins always require high sales turnover and a very small asset base.
options.d: Low turnover proves its price premium cannot increase profitability at any output level.

questions.text: A firm improves gross margin from 35% to 39%, but its net margin remains 8%. Which conclusion is most plausible?

options.a: The benefit was offset by other operating expenses, financing costs or taxes.
options.b: The firm necessarily reduced its average asset balance by exactly 4%.
options.c: The remaining expense categories must all have fallen as a percentage of revenue.
options.d: The gross margin and net margin changes are arithmetically incompatible.

questions.text: A retailer has revenue €2,000m, COGS €1,350m and SG&A €400m. If its net profit is €120m, the gross profit margin and net profit margin are:

Consider the statements.
I. Gross margin can decline if customers force selling-price discounts.
II. Gross margin can decline when input prices rise without matching sales-price increases.
III. Gross margin is determined solely by the debt-equity financing mix.
Which set is correct?

options.a: None of I, II or III
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A firm improves its net profit margin while its asset turnover falls so much that ROA declines. Which management conclusion is most consistent with DuPont?

options.a: The profit-margin improvement proves a stronger competitive position on its own.
options.b: Greater profitability per sale was outweighed by weaker sales generated per euro of assets.
options.c: The fall in turnover automatically increased equity regardless of financing.
options.d: Greater profitability per sale necessarily increased return on total assets.

questions.text: A consolidated company reports group net income €220m, of which €35m belongs to non-controlling interests. Average parent common equity is €925m, while average total equity is €1,100m. ROCE for parent common shareholders is:
Why can group ROE differ materially from return on common shareholders' equity (ROCE)?

options.a: ROCE automatically excludes all intangible assets from parent company equity.
options.b: Group income and equity include non-controlling claims not attributable to parent owners.
options.c: ROCE uses operating cash flow rather than earnings in every IFRS company.
options.d: ROE is calculated from annual sales while ROCE is calculated from stock price.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Financial leverage is average assets divided by average equity in the chapter.
II. At positive ROA, a higher equity multiplier raises ROE in the arithmetic identity.
III. Increased borrowing always makes operating assets more productive.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.d: I, II and III

questions.text: A firm reports sales growth of 15% and net-income growth of 45%, driven mainly by a large non-recurring asset gain. Which growth measure deserves attention for forecasting?

options.a: Growth in sustainable earnings after adjusting for transient gains.
options.b: Growth in total net income without adjustment for one-off gains.
options.c: Growth in the number of historical balance-sheet line items.
options.d: Growth in the unrealized market value of every fixed asset.

questions.text: An entity earns €240m, including a €70m unusual gain, and incurs €30m non-recurring restructuring costs. Assuming a simple pretax adjustment and no other items, normalized earnings are:
Normalized earnings increased from €180m to €200m, whereas reported net income rose from €175m to €240m. Approximate sustainable earnings growth equals:
A firm slows advertising and research activity to temporarily improve current earnings. Which potential forecasting error is most relevant?

options.a: Treating the temporary expense reduction as a durable improvement in economic profitability.
options.b: Treating the lower spending as an immediate rise in the firm's inventory balances.
options.c: Treating all advertising spending as a financing cash outflow from share repurchases.
options.d: Treating the lower spending as proof that no future product demand exists.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. All one-off charges must be counted as repeating operating expenses forever.
II. Excessive restructuring charges may distort measured earnings growth across years.
III. Deferred revenue can affect the timing of future recognized earnings.
Which set is correct?

options.a: None of I, II or III
options.d: I and II only

questions.text: A firm has current liabilities €300m, cash €30m, cash equivalents €30m, receivables €150m and inventory €240m. Assume these are all its current assets. Which ratios are correct?

options.a: Current 1.20; quick 0.70; cash 0.40
options.d: Current 1.50; quick 0.80; cash 0.20

questions.text: An otherwise unchanged company uses €40m of cash to pay €40m of current debt. Initial current assets are €200m and current liabilities €100m. The new current ratio is:
A company has negative net working capital but stable inventory replenishment and collects customer cash before paying suppliers. Which conclusion is most defensible?

options.a: Negative NWC proves its inventory has no resale value and must be written off fully.
options.b: Negative NWC is impossible when operating cash flows have remained positive.
options.c: Negative NWC may reflect its operating model, though liquidity risk still needs evaluation.
options.d: Negative NWC necessarily means it has already defaulted on every short-term obligation.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. The cash ratio is generally no higher than the quick ratio, with normal nonnegative assets.
II. A current ratio above one guarantees unlimited access to debt refinancing.
III. The current ratio may exceed the quick ratio because it includes inventories.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I, II and III
options.d: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A manufacturing firm has EBIT €180m, depreciation €45m, amortization €15m and gross interest expense €30m. Times interest earned and EBITDA coverage are:
A firm reports a very high EBITDA coverage ratio but only modest operating cash flow because receivables and inventories are rising rapidly. What is the main limitation of EBITDA coverage?

options.a: It directly includes every scheduled principal repayment, making CFO irrelevant.
options.b: It adds back non-cash charges but does not capture all cash tied up in working capital.
options.c: It deducts all working-capital investments from the numerator before calculating coverage.
options.d: It excludes depreciation, so it understates earnings available before interest.

questions.text: A company has current assets €500m, current liabilities €400m, total assets €1,000m, retained earnings €100m, EBIT €100m, equity market value €500m, total liabilities €500m and sales €1,000m. Approximate Altman Z-score is:

options.a: 1.18, the financial-distress zone in the lecture.
options.b: 3.18, the low-risk zone in the lecture.
options.c: 4.18, the low-risk zone in the lecture.
options.d: 1.84, the intermediate-risk zone in the lecture.
options.e: 2.18, the intermediate-risk zone in the lecture.

questions.text: A firm's Z-score increases from 1.3 to 3.2 while the assumptions behind the model remain comparable. Under the thresholds taught, what changes?

options.a: Its classification remains in the intermediate zone at both observed values.
options.b: Its classification moves from financial distress to the low-bankruptcy-risk zone.
options.c: Its classification moves from the low-risk zone to the financial-distress zone.
options.d: The model’s improved score guarantees that the company cannot subsequently default, independent of changes in its operating conditions.
options.e: The higher score means that an increasing fraction of sales must be financed by short-term borrowing.
options.f: Its Z-score is too high to be interpreted because the index cannot exceed three.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. The original Z-score includes a market-value-of-equity-to-liabilities component.
II. An Altman Z-score under 1.80 is classified as financially healthy in the slides.
III. A higher Altman Z-score generally indicates lower modeled bankruptcy risk.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.d: II and III only
options.f: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A company has negative EBIT, negative working capital and accumulated losses, but sales are still positive. Which interpretation of Altman's Z components is most appropriate?

options.a: Negative EBIT is omitted from Altman's model because profitability cannot be negative.
options.b: Several components can pull the overall score down despite a positive sales-to-assets contribution.
options.c: Positive sales guarantee a Z-score exceeding three regardless of the other inputs.
options.d: Accumulated losses automatically transform the market-value component into a positive profit.

questions.text: A company reports revenues €1,000m and average assets €400m. It improves asset turnover without changing revenues. What must have happened, within the ratio definition?

options.a: Gross profit margin necessarily increased.
options.d: Average reported assets decreased.

questions.text: A firm's ROE rises from 11% to 17%, while its ROA is unchanged and its leverage rises materially. Which analytical conclusion is strongest?

options.a: The ROE improvement proves higher margins and more productive asset use in equal proportions.
options.b: The ROE improvement may primarily reflect a higher equity multiplier rather than better operations.
options.c: The ROE improvement cannot occur without an equal increase in current operating cash flow.
options.d: The ROE improvement implies borrowing commitments and default risk have necessarily fallen.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A single historical growth rate uniquely determines a firm's future earnings growth.
II. Growth from sales can be decomposed by business segment.
III. Net income growth may be distorted by impairments and restructuring reversals.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.d: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A firm improves ROA from 8% to 10% while profit margin falls from 8% to 5%. What happened to asset turnover?

options.a: It rose from 1.0 to 1.5 times.
options.d: It rose from 1.6 to 2.0 times.

questions.text: A company with EBIT €50m and gross interest expense €25m doubles its debt at the same interest rate without changing EBIT. What happens to times interest earned?

options.a: It falls from 2.0 to 1.0.
options.d: It remains at 2.0 for both years.

questions.text: A business has CFO €160m, capital expenditure €100m and €400m interest-bearing debt. What is adjusted CFO-to-total-debt under the lecture's formula?
Which change would most likely make cross-company ROE comparisons misleading without further adjustment?

options.a: Both firms prepare accounts in the same accounting currency and year.
options.b: Both firms present liabilities and assets at the same reporting date.
options.c: Both firms have unchanged business models with stable capital structures.
options.d: One firm substantially changes its consolidated business mix through acquisitions.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A single ratio captures every qualitative dimension of a firm's competitive environment.
II. Reported accounting ratios may omit economically important unrecognized assets.
III. Conglomerates can complicate comparisons against single-industry peers.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.d: I, II and III
options.f: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A company's current ratio rises from 1.2 to 1.8 because large amounts of slow-moving inventory are acquired on long-term credit. What should the analyst do next?

options.a: Infer that debt service has improved because long-term obligations are excluded forever.
options.b: Treat the higher ratio as decisive evidence that all short-term obligations are safe.
options.c: Inspect inventory quality and liquid-asset coverage before declaring liquidity stronger.
options.d: Conclude that slow-moving merchandise is equivalent to immediately available cash.

questions.text: A retailer reduces DSO from 50 to 35 days but simultaneously reduces DPO from 70 to 48 days, while DIO is constant. What happens to CCC?

options.a: It increases by 7 days.
options.d: It remains unchanged because DSO and DPO both decreased.

questions.text: A company reports more net income this year but less sustainable income after removing unusual items. Which statement is best supported?

options.a: Reported earnings must be disregarded because the income statement is no longer IFRS-compliant.
options.b: Headline earnings growth may exaggerate the improvement in persistent operating performance.
options.c: The firm should immediately treat all discontinued gains as current inventory.
options.d: Future cash from operations necessarily grows at the headline net-income rate.

questions.text: A company has sales €1,400m, average total assets €700m, average equity €350m and net income €84m. Which triple is correct?

options.a: ROA 24%, ROE 12%, asset turnover 2.0.
options.d: ROA 12%, ROE 24%, asset turnover 1.5.

questions.text: An analyst's Z-score changes sharply following a major merger. What is the most responsible interpretation?

options.a: Infer that the model is invalid because Z-scores cannot be used across reporting periods.
options.b: Treat the change as proof that the merger created the same amount of additional cash flow.
options.c: Review changes in asset mix and reporting comparability before attributing the change to risk alone.
options.d: Conclude that the new score determines the firm's market value without separate analysis.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. The DuPont decomposition separates margin, turnover and leverage.
II. The gross profit margin is calculated using total book equity.
III. An increase in debt necessarily improves operating asset turnover.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.d: I only

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A low quick ratio may coexist with a current ratio above one.
II. Improving ROE through leverage can raise financial risk.
III. A firm's Z-score integrates profitability, liquidity and other factors.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.d: II only
